note: THREE MEASURED FACTS ABOUT THE WALK BAND, from The Rhumb Task 1. 1: EVERY ROOM OFFERS EXACTLY 3 OF 8 COMPASS DIRECTIONS, and which 3 depends on the orientation of the triangle you stand on. Measured 3 of 8 refused from the seed-42 flagship (n, ne, s refused; e, se, sw, w, nw moved), and confirmed structurally in exits_of, which labels each of a rooms three edge-neighbours with its true geodesic bearing bucketed to 8 points. There is no sequence of go e that walks east. 2: NOTHING BLOCKS LATERAL MOVEMENT OUTDOORS. Session::go performs no biome, water or passability check of any kind, and exits_of never filters exits by biome, so marine rooms are already in the walk graph. The only lateral refusal a walking player has ever seen is No way X from here, which is about the tiling, not the world. SUBMERGED_LATERAL_REFUSAL is orthogonal and gated on being already submerged. 3: NAIVE FIXED-PRIORITY-DIRECTION WALKING TRAPS IN A CLOSED 6-ROOM CYCLE. Always trying n, then ne, then e and taking the first that resolves gets stuck in a 6-room loop, reproducible in both rotational orders, on a mesh that is FULLY CONNECTED: a randomised-order walk from the same start reached 506 plus distinct rooms immediately. This is a strategy artifact, not a connectivity defect, but any keep-heading-X player behaviour can get stuck today. Evidence: a 300,000-room DFS from the seed-42 flagship, all tropical rainforest, never left the landmass.
